holidays.name: Find a Rainbow Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to looking up, chasing a little sunshine through the rain, and spotting a rainbow wherever one may be hiding. Pots of gold are optional, but smiles are encouraged.
holidays.origin: Find a Rainbow Day is an unofficial observance that appears on quirky holiday calendars, tied to the early spring showers that make rainbows more likely in many places.
holidays.funFact: Every rainbow is actually a full circle, but from the ground the horizon cuts off the bottom half. From an airplane you can sometimes see the whole thing.

holidays.name: Tweed Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the sturdy, scratchy, wonderfully dapper woolen fabric. Fans are encouraged to dust off their tweed jackets, flat caps, and waistcoats and channel their inner countryside professor.
holidays.origin: Tweed Day is a fashion observance that honors Scotland's rich textile history. Tweed is traditionally associated with the Scottish Borders and the River Tweed, and Harris Tweed is a protected product.
holidays.funFact: The name 'tweed' is often said to come from a misreading of the Scots word 'tweel' (twill) as 'tweed,' possibly influenced by the River Tweed.

holidays.name: World Party Day
holidays.description: A global excuse to throw a party, with the only requirement being that you celebrate. Balloons, snacks, and dancing in the kitchen all count as valid participation.
holidays.origin: World Party Day is an unofficial observance that began as a way to encourage people to come together and celebrate life with friends, family, and neighbors on the same day.
holidays.funFact: The word 'party' comes from the Old French 'partie,' meaning a part or group, which originally referred to a group of people taking one side of a matter.

holidays.name: Don't Go to Work Unless It's Fun Day
holidays.description: A cheeky holiday that encourages people to ditch the grind unless their job sparks joy. It's a day to think about whether work is fun, and if not, how to make it so.
holidays.origin: This tongue-in-cheek observance comes from the world of unofficial holidays, promoting a lighthearted reminder to find joy in your profession.
holidays.funFact: Studies on workplace happiness regularly find that people who report having a close friend at work are more engaged and more likely to enjoy their job.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Mousse Day
holidays.description: A day to indulge in the airy, silky, spoonable dessert that makes you feel fancy even when you eat it straight out of the fridge at midnight.
holidays.origin: A food holiday honoring the French dessert, whose name means 'foam' or 'lather' in French. The modern version is often credited to 18th and 19th century French cooking traditions.
holidays.funFact: Some historians credit the painter Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec with popularizing a 'mayonnaise of chocolate' in the 1890s, a precursor to modern mousse.
